matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the difference between the two sides; this guides which sticks need to be moved.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before enumerating possible moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping numeric verification and assuming the equation X = XI + I is already correct.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate all ways a single stick can be moved from any character to any other character, respecting the shapes of Roman numerals and operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only considering moves from operators and ignoring possible moves from numerals like I, missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the involved symbols change and check whether the net change matches the required discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During evaluation of each candidate transformation.
matchstick.example: Choosing a move that changes X (10) to V (5) when the needed change is +2, leading to an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat '=' as two horizontal sticks; moving one of them can turn it into '-' (single horizontal), and adding a horizontal to '-' can restore '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests that changing the equality sign to a subtraction (or vice versa) could balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn '=' into '+' by moving a stick, which is impossible.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical yields '-', removing the horizontal yields 'I', and adding a vertical to '-' creates '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting operators could resolve the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' to get '-', but not placing the removed stick elsewhere, leaving an orphan stick.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' to swap them).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both operators are present and a single stick move can adjust both to satisfy the equation.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-' but leaving the source '=' as a single horizontal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the needed numeric change matches the value increase obtainable by adding a stick to a numeral (e.g., adding a vertical to I to make II), move a stick from an operator to that numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy can be fixed by increasing a numeral's value using a stick taken from an operator.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to I to make II but forgetting to adjust the operator, leaving the operator invalid.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation (source may become empty)
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, the target must become a valid numeral or operator; the source character may become empty (i.e., disappear) if that results in a syntactically valid equation, especially when the source is a single‑stick numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moves that involve removing a stick from a single‑stick numeral or from a character that can be omitted without breaking the expression.
matchstick.example: Rejecting the move that takes the only stick from I in 'XI' and places it after X, because the source I would disappear, even though the resulting equation 'XI = X + I' is valid.

matchstick.title: Numeral elimination via stick removal
matchstick.principle: A numeral consisting of a single stick (I) can be eliminated by moving its stick elsewhere; the numeral disappears, and the equation must remain syntactically correct (no dangling operators).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by the value of a single‑stick numeral, consider removing that numeral by moving its stick to another location.
matchstick.example: Assuming the I must stay after moving its stick, missing the solution where the I is removed, yielding 'XI = X + I'.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often moves a stick without checking that the original character still forms a recognized Roman numeral or operator, resulting in shapes like a lone diagonal or an empty space.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that both the source and destination characters correspond to a valid numeral or operator; if the source becomes empty, ensure this is allowed (e.g., single‑stick numeral elimination).

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may generate a transformed equation but forget to recompute the integer values, assuming the move fixes the equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values of both sides after applying a stick move and confirm they are equal before output.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may inadvertently delete an operator or numeral, producing a malformed expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the original sequence of symbols; ensure that any character that loses a stick either remains a valid symbol or is intentionally removed as a whole numeral, and that operators still have operands on both sides.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing '+' to '-' or '=' to '-' alters the arithmetic operation, but the model may not adjust the numeric calculation accordingly.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is altered, recalculate the expression using the new operator to check if equality holds.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes adds or removes sticks instead of relocating a single stick, violating the puzzle constraint.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the exact stick being moved: remove it from one character and place it onto another; never create or destroy sticks.
